case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread focuses on Bluetooth SIG qualification and declaration handling for multiple Bluetooth products using existing QDIDs and BLE modules. The customer asks about declaration version mismatches, Product List expansion registration, and DID-related registration handling. The consultant explains how declaration versions are automatically inherited from linked QDIDs and clarifies when additional Product List registrations can be added without additional fees. The exchange also includes correction of mistaken QDID linkages and cleanup of temporary model-name data before final registration confirmation.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: A central discussion concerns Bluetooth specification version inheritance from a linked QDID. The consultant explains that a declaration linked to a QDID registered as Bluetooth 5.1 will automatically become a Bluetooth 5.1 declaration and cannot be manually edited to 5.0. The consultant further explains that Bluetooth 5.1 mainly adds optional functionality over Bluetooth 5.0 and does not introduce additional mandatory features, making 5.1 registration acceptable for products using only 5.0-level functionality. Another key topic is reuse-based Product List expansion, where derivative products using the same BLE module and Host Stack can be added through the web process without additional registration fees. The consultant also clarifies that proving Host Stack sameness does not require formal submission to the Bluetooth SIG and is left to the applicant company's own technical judgment.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The consultant's reasoning is driven by Bluetooth SIG declaration linkage rules and reuse principles. The linked QDID determines the declaration specification version automatically, so the declaration version cannot be independently edited once the QDID is selected. Reuse eligibility for expanded Product List registrations depends on whether the BLE module and Host Stack remain unchanged from the already registered implementation. Administrative registration details such as model names and linked references must also be corrected before final submission because review-page information becomes part of the formal qualified listing.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Using the wrong QDID linkage can cause the declaration to inherit an unintended Bluetooth specification version that cannot later be manually corrected. Incorrect assumptions about reuse eligibility could lead to improper Product List expansion or inaccurate qualification claims. Failing to verify review-page metadata such as model names and linked registrations before finalization can result in incorrect public listings and additional correction work after publication. Misunderstanding the automatic linkage behavior between QDIDs and declarations could also delay customer approval and qualification completion.
case_analysis.consulting_mistake: The consultant acknowledged that two registrations were initially linked to the wrong reference targets, which caused the displayed Bluetooth specification versions to be reversed. The consultant corrected the QDID linkage mappings, updated the review pages, and explained why the remaining declaration still had to remain at Bluetooth 5.1 because the linked QDID itself was registered as 5.1. The thread demonstrates the importance of validating QDID linkage assignments before generating final declaration review pages.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: In Bluetooth qualification consulting, the linked QDID is the authoritative driver for declaration behavior, including displayed specification version. Consultants should validate QDID mappings, reuse assumptions, Host Stack equivalence, and public listing metadata before final submission because many declaration properties become fixed or automatically inherited once the linkage is established.
